    Start · The rhythm

    How a Day Runs

    The weekday rhythm from 7:00 to 19:00 ET, the weekend horizons, what runs on its own versus on request, mock mode versus AI mode, and where each session shows up in the app.

    The rhythm at a glance#

    Bablytics runs on a scheduler (APScheduler, all jobs in America/New_York). On a weekday the board meets four times — briefing, pre-open, midday, court — and two engines work the session in between: the Pulse every thirty minutes and the Bailiff every fifteen. Bookkeeping happens at 16:45. The weekend belongs to the horizon reviews. Every job below also has a button, so you never have to wait for the clock to see any of it.

    Weekday, hour by hour#

    7:00

    The Morning Briefing#

    The pipeline first records any newly elapsed 1-day and 5-day outcomes and retrains the prediction model, then scans the S&P 500 universe for options-volume spikes, pulls US and world headlines, congressional disclosures and the cycle decomposition, fetches chart technicals and value stats per candidate, and hands ~40 candidates to the board. Thirteen seats grade every candidate; the Skeptic rebuts with all grades in hand; the Executive ranks a Top 20 — ten option leads, each with a selected contract at least six days from expiry, and ten stock leads — and writes the memo with the day's house rules. After the run, the Paper League opens each seat's positions and, if you have connected a broker, the bot stages (never submits) up to five orders. Page: Morning Briefing.

    9:15

    The Pre-Open Check#

    Fifteen minutes before the bell the whole committee — the thirteen graders and the Skeptic — re-reads the briefing against the overnight tape: the futures board, each lead's pre-market print versus its briefing price, an audit of whether yesterday's option volume converted into held open interest, the morning's analyst upgrades and downgrades, the 8:30–9:00 economic prints and fresh flagged headlines. Each panelist files a market read — confirmed move, pump fake or undecided — and a per-lead action (hold, exit, trim, upgrade, watch). The Executive signs the verdict and a memo update; the per-lead orders show as corner chips on the lead cards. Page: Pre-Open Check.

    9:30

    The session opens: Pulse and Bailiff#

    From 9:30 to 16:00 the Pulse runs a cycle at :00 and :30 — fourteen cycles a day — blending the board's standing views (last evening's court, the briefing, the pre-open, the midday) with the vote of five actor-critic models into a bounded lean per position: enter, add, hold, trim or exit, with an ATR exit zone and a paragraph about your book. The Bailiff watches every fifteen minutes, pricing the board's written invalidations against the tape on the right basis; a “closes below” ruling stays pending until the close no matter what the intraday tick says. Both are research output with no execution path. Pages: The Pulse, The Bailiff.

    12:30

    The Midday Check-In#

    Three hours in, the same committee reconvenes over the midday tape — each lead's move from its briefing entry, the market context, fresh headlines — and, the point of the meeting, each member's own open Paper League positions marked at midday. Every member files a read, a risk tilt (risk up, risk down, unchanged) and exactly one hold-or-close per open position; every close is executed on the paper ledger at the midday mark. The Executive synthesizes a headline and a board tilt. Page: Midday Check-In.

    14:35

    The Bailiff's ratchet check#

    The standing crude settle rail is evaluated and the result is reported — BANK-HALF or no action. Nothing is executed, because “bank half” is a sizing decision the record cannot infer. A docket line is written only when the Bailiff is in enforcement mode.

    16:05

    The close sweep#

    With the closes printed, the Bailiff runs its close-basis pass: this is where “closes below” rulings can fire. In the default dry-run mode it looks and reports; with bailiff_dry_run set to 0 it closes the leg in the record — the board's book and the Paper League — and writes the event.

    16:45

    Outcomes, League mark, model training#

    For every past lead whose 1- or 5-trading-day horizon has elapsed, the realized return is recorded (sign-flipped for shorts). The Paper League is marked to market — pending entries priced, five-day holds closed, every equity curve re-derived from the ledger. Then the outcome model retrains: a small scikit-learn network (MLPRegressor(32, 16)) that predicts the 5-day return from the thirteen member grades plus numeric features, once at least 25 leads have realized outcomes. Page: Learning Loops.

    19:00

    The Evening Court#

    The day's leads are scored against the close (option leads have their chosen contract repriced), the Pyramid re-forms on the realized returns, and every one of the fifteen seats writes a self-review — on base, off base, the lesson — seeing only its own morning grades next to the returns. The Executive reviews against the full standings and reads your trade reflections verbatim. Entries are persisted to the journals, the per-member dossiers are regenerated, and then the court runs the night's model generation (when rl_evolve_enabled is on) and reports what training did — or why it did not run. Page: Evening Court.

    Saturday and Sunday: the horizons#

    One engine, two directions, three horizons, layered over the daily loop:

    • Saturday 8:00 — the Week in Review (backward): lead performance over the just-ended Monday–Sunday week with realized outcomes, windowed per-member accuracy, Pyramid movement, Paper League equity deltas, the econ tape, and your own scorecard built from taken trades and reflections.
    • Sunday 15:00 — the weekly deep generation: the same score → train → breed → select cycle as the nightly court generation, with a deeper budget (5 min per member, 30 min total), behind the same held-out gate and the same rl_evolve_enabled switch. It is not a retrain from scratch — that is train.py's job, run by hand.
    • Sunday 17:00 — the Week Ahead (forward): a prospectus from the current market context, cycle read, the upcoming econ calendar, the carried book and open paper positions, sector posture and the Pyramid leader's read.
    • Month and year editions ride two daily guard jobs: 18:00 runs the month in review on the last calendar day of a month (the year in review on December 31), and 7:30 runs the month-ahead prospectus on the first (the year-ahead on January 1). On every other day the guards pass silently.

    The panel rotates by horizon — week: Executive, Croupier, Timekeeper, Skeptic and the current Pyramid leader; month and year: Executive, Croupier, Timekeeper, Oracle, Graham, Black Swan. Reports land on the Reviews tab with run-now buttons and encrypted PDF export; a fresh weekend report also gets a dashboard strip. Page: Reviews & Horizons.

    Automatic versus on request#

    Every scheduled session has a button, and the guards are the same either way: the morning pipeline refuses to double-run a completed day unless forced, the pre-open and midday skip a run they already reviewed (their buttons force a fresh one), the court skips a run it already journaled (its button forces a fresh set of entries), and locks prevent concurrent runs. Times come from the settings table and are re-read on reschedule; the Settings page exposes the morning, pre-open and evening times directly, while the others are stored under the keys below.

    What never runs on its own.

    No job places, stages or submits an order except the morning run's staging step, and that step only fills a queue you review. Broker submission is one click per order behind a confirmation, and there is no setting that changes that. The Bailiff ships dry: until you set bailiff_dry_run to 0, a scheduled pass changes nothing in the database.

    Mock mode versus AI mode#

    The rule is one line in config.py: if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is empty, or BABLYTICS_MOCK=1 (legacy STONKS_MOCK=1), the app is in mock mode. Every session then runs end to end with deterministic heuristic board members instead of model calls — zero API cost, demoable offline — and the UI shows a mock mode pill so you always know which board you are talking to.

    What mock mode does
    Each persona grades from simple rules in its own spirit — Flow keys off volume-to-open-interest ratios, Dagger off RSI and momentum, Sam punishes counter-trend setups, the Skeptic inverts the room's mean, the Executive takes a weighted blend with the Pyramid leader's grades at 1.5× — with small per-ticker jitter so output looks alive. The output shape is identical to real mode. Court entries are deterministic but data-true, built from each member's best- and worst-aligned calls; Pulse rationales are templates that interpolate the real numbers. If even the market scan fails (fully offline), the scanner falls back to a synthetic candidate list so the pipeline still demonstrates end to end.
    What AI mode does
    Each seat is a structured-output call to the Anthropic model named by BABLYTICS_MODEL (default claude-opus-4-8), seeded with the persona's system prompt, its five most recent journal lessons and its Pyramid rank. The morning board is fifteen calls (thirteen graders, the Skeptic, the Executive); the pre-open and midday are one call per panelist plus one for the Executive; the court is one call per seat; a Pulse cycle is one call for the rationale. Any failed call falls back to the mock text for that member, so a session always completes.
    How to switch
    Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… in your .env and restart. From a checkout that is the repo-root .env; the desktop app reads a .env in its data folder (~/Library/Application Support/Bablytics/.env on macOS, %APPDATA%\Bablytics\.env on Windows, ~/.local/share/bablytics/.env on Linux). The key is read once at start-up — there is no settings-table field for it — so a restart is required, and BABLYTICS_MOCK=1 forces mock mode even with a key present. Details: Download & Install, Run from Source.

    Where each session shows up#

    Dashboard · MORNING BRIEFING
    The memo (with the Listen control), the market strip, the Pyramid leader strip, the twenty lead cards with entry / now / stop / target, the pre-open banner and its corner chips, the midday card, the Bailiff card, the staged-orders pill when the queue is non-empty, and the reflections-due banner.
    Dashboard · EVENING COURT
    The close-of-day index strip and regime, best- and worst-call callouts, the scoreboard (briefing price → close, direction-adjusted return, option contracts at their last price) and “The Court Speaks” — one card per seat with ON BASE / OFF BASE / LESSON. The toggle is also the day/night theme switch.
    Pulse
    Goals, the countdown to the next cycle, your book's cards with leans and exit zones, the watch table over the lead pool, and the Model card with the population's state.
    Boardroom
    The roster, the Pyramid with its crown, every seat's JOURNAL strip, and the “Run evening review” button. Each seat links to its member workspace and dossier.
    League
    The fifteen paper books, sortable by window, with equity sparklines, the midday adjustments and the last-action feed.
    Reviews
    The weekend, month and year reports — timeline, report view, run-now, encrypted PDF.
    Archive
    Every past day in one place: the briefing, the pre-open, the midday, the court, the journals, the Bailiff dockets and the realized 1d/5d columns. Page: News, Library & Archive.
    PDF
    Both dashboard modes export — the morning briefing and the evening court (market at the close, the scoreboard, the per-member ON BASE / OFF BASE / LESSON sections) — as password-encrypted PDFs. The run-history / last-seven / five-day / models appendix appears only in the live-board court document built in the day folder.
